bypass_b2_quoted_verbatim.title: A landing on a side branch is acknowledged and stamped ancestor_of_main
bypass_b2_quoted_verbatim.detail: No forgery required. A genuine proof minted on a genuine transport bound to Target('openclaw-onboarding', branch='side') is accepted by ack() of a queue for that repository, and the written ack block asserts 'ancestor_of_main': 'proven' while ack.proof.target.branch is literally 'side'. The store records an ancestry claim about main that nothing ever tested.
bypass_b2_quoted_verbatim.anchor: CONTROL/queue_ack.py ack() line 248 compares only valid.target.repository to self.repository -- repository string only, never branch or remote. Line 305 then writes ancestor_of_main unconditionally. QueueStore.__init__ takes a repository and no branch, so nothing in the module ever constrains the branch.
bypass_b2_quoted_verbatim.fix_direction_quoted: Bind the store to (repository, branch) and compare the proof's full Target, not just the repository string; or drop the ancestor_of_main claim and record the branch actually proven.

arbiter_scope_ruling_quoted_verbatim.quote: Exception, and it is a real deliverable defect but bounded: BYPASS-B2's stamp. `queue_ack.py:305` writes `"ancestor_of_main": f"proven ..."` unconditionally, so a genuine proof minted on `Target('openclaw-onboarding', branch='side')` gets an ancestry claim about main that nothing tested. That overstatement is produced by the module itself, not by a lying caller. It is a one-line bounded fix (bind the store to (repository, branch) and compare the full Target, or record the branch actually proven), and it does not remove any of the row's four clauses from the deliverable.

defect_fixed.what_changed_in_one_line: QueueStore is now bound to a full IP.Target (repository, remote, branch), a proof for any other target is refused wrong-target, and the ack block records proven_target while asserting ancestor_of_main only when origin/main was the branch actually proven.

three_edits.after: def __init__(self, path, repository, branch="main", remote="origin"): self.target = IP.Target(repository, remote=remote, branch=branch); self.repository = self.target.repository
three_edits.effect: the store declares which target it receives landings for, so a branch or remote it never tested cannot arrive as evidence about it

three_edits.after: if valid.target != self.target: raise AckRefused("wrong-target", f"proof is for {repository!r} on {remote}/{branch}; this queue is ...")
three_edits.effect: full-Target comparison; a main-bound queue refuses a landing proven on a side branch, with the store byte-untouched

three_edits.after: "proven_target": fresh.target.as_dict()  ... plus: if (fresh.target.remote, fresh.target.branch) == ("origin", "main"): entry["ack"]["ancestor_of_main"] = f"proven ..."
three_edits.effect: the branch actually proven is always recorded, and the main ancestry claim is written only when that branch really was origin/main -- a claim that cannot be true is never written

defect_fixed.why_both_halves: The arbiter offered 'bind the store to (repository, branch) and compare the full Target' OR 'record the branch actually proven'. Both are implemented because they answer different halves: binding stops a side-branch landing from being acknowledged into a main queue at all, recording keeps the acknowledged block truthful for a queue that IS bound to a non-main branch, where no main claim can be made. The round-2 verifier's own B2 probe demanded outright refusal, which the binding satisfies.
